findings.issue: isEnabled puts the FLAG_<KEY> env override first and exempts it from the phase guard in RUN_MODE=local, and a pass criterion requires FLAG_RESALE_BOARD=on under PHASE=P1 to read on. A21 (lines 71, 160, 170) requires the opposite (A08.1): in local an override of a licence-bound or phase flag may only force off, and with every FLAG_<KEY>=on set every licence-bound flag must still read off through isEnabled. The same order also lets FLAG_AGENTS_TRAFFIC=on (or FLAG_PLATFORM_INFLOW_FREEZE=off) in .env beat A48's kill switch set through A21's database source. An operator kill switch then has no effect in any stack that carries the override, and a correct A08 build makes A21's gate fail.
findings.fix: Adopt A08.1. In RUN_MODE=local an env override can only move a flag towards its safe state: off for phase and licence-bound flags and for agents.traffic, on for platform.inflow_freeze and platform.marketplace_suspend. It never overrides a source answer in the permissive direction. A permissive override is honoured only in RUN_MODE=test, stays subject to the phase guard unless the test also sets PHASE, and is logged at start-up. Replace the pass criterion with three tests: FLAG_RESALE_BOARD=on in local reads off; in test it reads on and is logged; FLAG_AGENTS_TRAFFIC=on with a stub source answering off reads off in both modes.

findings.issue: The kms key-use table is closed, oracle-frozen and 'reopens this spec' on any change, yet it lacks what the dependent specs already require. (a) Only bootstrap may call createKey and no one may call rotateKey. But A15 creates its own V1-V3, V4, V7 and attestation keys through kms.createKey (A23 confirms this), and A04's enc() creates tenant keys on first use and rotates them (N20). (b) Rows other specs need are missing: A22's idv-result-attestation, idv-webhook-secret and idv-sandbox-data (identities identity and sanctions); A17's bank webhook secret and field encryption; A29's bundler-submitter EOA key; A101's IP-prefix HMAC key; A102's backup, erasure-seal and backup-attest (P-256) keys. (c) There is no hmac verb, although A17, A22, A46 and A101 all use HMAC. getSecret has no way to create a secret-value and no caller allowed to use it. (d) A 'paymaster' identity may sign paymaster-v7 through a lint path that is never defined ('the module the wallet node names'). A29 says paymaster/sponsor holds no key and asks A15 to sign under its AUTO approval, so this is an undefined second signer for V7. (e) The 'webhooks' lint path is not concrete. (f) A22 relies on deterministic ES256 (RFC 6979) from the sandbox kms, which A08 never states. The oracle would freeze a table under which A04, A15, A17, A22, A29, A101 and A102 fail at runtime with KEY_USE_NOT_PERMITTED, or must widen the policy themselves.
findings.fix: Freeze the full table with the permitted verbs per identity. custody: createKey, sign and rotateKey on approval-attestation, vault-v1..v3, identity-agent-v4, paymaster-v7, deployer and guardian. db: createKey, generateDataKey, encrypt, decrypt and rotateKey on db-column. storage: the same verbs on storage-data. identity and sanctions: A22's three rows. bank: bank-webhook-secret and bank-field-data. bundler: sign on bundler-submitter. webhooks: path services/api/src/modules/integrations/. agent-guard: A101's ip-prefix-hmac. backup: A102's three purposes. bootstrap: createKey and publicKey only. Drop the paymaster identity so custody alone signs paymaster-v7. Add hmac and verifyHmac verbs so secrets never leave kms, and either add createSecret or remove getSecret. State that sandbox ECDSA uses RFC 6979 deterministic nonces on both curves. Map every lint identity to a concrete owned path taken from final-graph.json. Add a pass criterion that a fixture caller at each mapped path exercises every row.

findings.issue: A21 builds against A08's 'OverrideSource interface', and A12, A48 and A104 call isEnabled on hot paths, but A08 never defines that interface: no registration function, no method signature, no answer type (on, off or no answer), and no statement of whether isEnabled is sync or async. A21 needs a revert made in the worker to be seen on the next API read. A08 also describes the source as 'resolving vehicle, then tenant, then platform scope'. That reads as narrowest-scope-first-wins and contradicts A21's rule that the effective state is the AND of the scopes.
findings.fix: Freeze registerOverrideSource(source) and interface OverrideSource { resolve(key, ctx): Promise<'on'|'off'|undefined> }. Make isEnabled(key, ctx) return Promise<boolean>, or define a sync snapshot variant with a stated freshness contract. Delete the scope-order sentence and say scope combination is the source's rule (A21 uses AND). Add pass criteria that a second registration throws and that an undefined answer falls through to the default.

findings.issue: The chain allow-list depends circularly on a node that is not a dependency. A08 accepts 'a host listed in A07's TOOLCHAIN.md Base Sepolia list', and a pass criterion requires CHAIN_ALLOW_LIST to equal A07's contracts/TOOLCHAIN.md lists. Yet A07 writes TOOLCHAIN.md as a copy of A08's lists, and A07 is not in A08's deps (A01, A02). A08's gate can therefore fail on A07's build state, the 'single source' actually has two sources, and reading TOOLCHAIN.md at runtime crosses A07's owned path. A07 also still says '*.base.org'.
findings.fix: Freeze CHAIN_ALLOW_LIST as a literal inside A08: chain 31337 with hosts localhost, 127.0.0.1, ::1 and chain; chain 84532 with sepolia.base.org, only with TESTNET_OPT_IN=A86. Adding a host reopens A08. Remove the TOOLCHAIN.md reference and the equality criterion from A08, and leave the equality assertion to A23, which depends on both nodes. Flag A07 to replace '*.base.org' with the exact list.

findings.issue: The prior oracle and estimate finding is fixed only in the note. The frontmatter says oracle: yes and 8-12 agent-hours, but final-graph.json still has oracle false and est 4-6 for A08. The generator writes the frontmatter and the gauntlet schedule from the graph, so the next regeneration reverts A08 to a non-oracle node. The hidden kms authority suite (attestation, vault and paymaster keys) might then not be written before the build.
findings.fix: Set oracle: true, est_lo 8 and est_hi 12 for A08 in final-graph.json and app-graph.json, then regenerate the totals and the critical path. Add a generator check that fails when a note's frontmatter and the graph disagree on oracle or estimate.

findings.issue: The no-process-env rule (lint plus the no-production test) exempts only contracts/hardhat.config.ts, scripts/ and infra/. Other nodes' own files legitimately touch env: A52's next.config.ts reads REALX_DEV_TOOLS; A52 and A53 own next.config.ts, middleware.ts and playwright.config.ts; vitest and Playwright configs and test setup files set env for child processes; A08's own tests spawn processes with RUN_MODE=production. In addition, loadConfig parses every section at once, so a Next build stage or a one-shot such as kms-init would need every other node's required variables. The test is either red on a clean tree or the builder quietly narrows it.
findings.fix: List the exact exemptions: apps/*/next.config.ts, **/playwright.config.ts, **/vitest.config.ts, and test setup files that only write env. Alternatively export withTestEnv() and readBuildEnv(section) from packages/config and require those files to use them. Add loadConfig({ sections }) so a process validates only the sections it uses and still reports every error in them. Add a pass criterion that the clean tree, with a fixture copying A52's next.config.ts pattern, passes the rule.

findings.issue: A health pass criterion requires the AdapterHealth zod fields to be 'exactly the ADM-32 connector columns'. The product-map ADM-32 connector table has three columns (Connector, State, Latency), while AdapterHealth has seven fields, so the criterion cannot be met as written.
findings.fix: Require instead that the schema equals the field list frozen in §1, and add a mapping table (Connector from name, State from status plus lastError, Latency from latencyMs) showing A76 can render ADM-32 without another mapping layer.

findings.issue:
The sandbox locations disagree with A23. A08 puts the dev master key in the docker secret realx_kms_master and the keystore in the realx_kms volume. A23 (lines 53-59) forbids the secret bind mount, keeps the master key file in the realx_kms volume at /var/lib/realx/kms/dev-master.key, and puts the keystore under realx_sandbox at partitions/

/kms/. A23 expects A08 to align.
findings.fix:
Rewrite §3 to match A23. The master key path is KMS_SANDBOX_MASTER_KEY_FILE: in compose /var/lib/realx/kms/dev-master.key in the realx_kms volume; on the host the default %LOCALAPPDATA%\RealX\kms\dev-master.key. The keystore lives under STORAGE_SANDBOX_ROOT/partitions/

/kms/, which in compose is the realx_sandbox volume. Drop the docker-secret wording.

findings.issue: Several behaviours have no defined input or break layering. The EICAR stub matches on 'a name containing EICAR', but putObject and presignUpload take no file name. The health criterion needs a 'stopped adapter', but nothing defines a stop verb. The core config section validates ADAPTER_<NAME> for every manifest name, which makes packages/config and adapters/core depend on each other. forCaller(identity) takes an identity the caller asserts itself, so misuse is caught only by lint, not at runtime.
findings.fix: Either add an optional fileName to putObject and presignUpload or drop the name rule. Add stop() and start() to the echo adapter or to SandboxControl. Have adapters/core register the ADAPTER_* variables through defineConfigSection. Give each adapter a kms handle pre-bound to its manifest name through the factory ctx, and keep forCaller only for the non-adapter identities.
